title: Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a system that translates a quantitative description of a desired biological function into genetic instructions that reliably produce that function in a specified host organism and environment. A specification could describe how a circuit should respond to an input or how a pathway should produce an output. The target is predictable behavior of the assembled system, including interactions among its components and with the host.

Functional sequence generation provides an experimental foundation. The supplied Evo study reports generated anti-CRISPR proteins and interacting toxin–antitoxin systems, demonstrating that genomic language models can produce active components and small biological systems. Predictive circuit and pathway design would extend this capability from generating and screening promising sequences to reliably satisfying explicit system-level requirements.

Scope synthesis: the intended capability covers multiple design classes and several explicitly identified hosts and conditions. Success in one chassis would establish performance in that tested setting; portability would require additional evidence. The concept does not require designing an entire organism or imply that any imaginable biological function is physically achievable.

significance.text: Reliable specification-to-function design could make biological engineering substantially more systematic. The direct advance would be obtaining reproducible, measurable circuit and pathway behavior with less experimental selection and redesign. The Evo study provides a relevant starting point because it demonstrates functional generated systems while also documenting the continuing need for computational filtering and experimental testing. How much a predictive design system reduces design–build–test cycles would need to be measured against existing workflows.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more dependable production pathways, programmable cellular responses, and biological systems intended for therapeutic or environmental use. These applications would require separate demonstrations of performance, stability and suitability under their actual operating conditions. Reliable circuit design alone would not establish a successful industrial process, treatment or environmental intervention.

Interpretive synthesis: the revolutionary change would be a more dependable relationship between a requested function and the biological system built to perform it. An analogy to compiling software is useful only within limits: the host is an active biological context, and a design's demonstrated operating range would remain part of its specification. The supplied record does not establish an effect size for reduced iteration or provide historical breakthrough comparisons that would calibrate the magnitude of the impact.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability targeted here is reliable prediction of the behavior of interacting designed components, followed by design choices that meet quantitative requirements in a specified host and environment. The supplied study demonstrates useful component and small-system generation, but explicitly retains computational filtering and experimental validation. It therefore does not establish broad, reliable specification-driven design or experimental portability across chassis.

Engineering synthesis: the design process would need to connect sequence choices to component activity, component interactions and the resulting system-level behavior. It would also need to distinguish specifications it can satisfy confidently from those requiring more evidence or redesign. Generating individually active proteins is insufficient if their combined behavior misses the required output, timing or robustness.

The proposed scope includes effects of host context, competition for cellular resources and environmental conditions. These are design concerns retained from the research, but the supplied study does not directly substantiate the resource-competition and environmental-dependence assertions. Their importance, quantitative contribution and treatment by a general design method remain questions for further evidence. The supplied record also cannot determine whether the full capability remained unavailable across the field as of 1 November 2026.

current_state.text: Merchant, King, Nguyen and Hie's “Semantic design of functional de novo genes from a genomic language model” was published online on 19 November 2025, with a January 2026 issue date. The supplied review identifies experimental results for Evo-generated anti-CRISPR proteins and type II and type III toxin–antitoxin systems. These are demonstrated functional sequences and small systems, rather than solely computational predictions. They do not constitute a demonstration of broad predictive circuit or pathway design.

For a type II toxin–antitoxin example, the researchers first identified an active generated toxin, EvoRelE1, and then generated antitoxin candidates. When co-expressed with EvoRelE1, 50% of the tested generated antitoxin candidates rescued cell growth. This supports the design of functionally interacting components, while the staged procedure matters: it does not establish that complete systems can routinely be generated successfully in a single initial submission.

The paper reports experimental success rates of 17–50% when testing tens of variants. Those rates describe tested candidates after selection, not the fraction of all raw generations that succeeded. The anti-CRISPR methods, for example, describe selecting 84 candidates for further screening from a pool of 131. Filtering, candidate selection and experimental screening must therefore be included when interpreting the reported design efficiency.

EvoAcr1 and EvoAcr2 reportedly lacked significant sequence matches to proteins in OpenGenome or BLAST nr and showed activity in liquid-culture and phage assays. Their sequence novelty is relative to the databases and search procedures reported, including BLAST searches dated 14 July 2025; it is not proof that no corresponding sequence exists anywhere in nature. Low-confidence predicted structures also limit conclusions about structural novelty.

The reviewed evidence principally concerns prokaryotic sequence design and functional assays in E. coli. Computational recovery of sequences associated with other organisms does not establish experimental portability into those organisms. The paper's suggestion that multicomponent generation could accelerate circuit, pathway or genome development is a prospective implication, not an experimentally established achievement at those broader scales.

The supplied evidence is incomplete: the retained PDF extraction was truncated, some pages had no extractable text, and figures and omitted material were not independently inspected in the supplied review. The explicit results and methods available support the bounded findings above, but cannot resolve every methodological question. The freshness record is empty, so subsequent progress and field-wide capability as of 1 November 2026 remain unassessed; these access and coverage limits do not show that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: prospectively generate multiple distinct genetic circuits and pathways from quantitative specifications for several named host organisms and environmental conditions. Before testing, define the design classes, host–condition combinations, functional acceptance thresholds, robustness requirements and acceptable failure rates. These would be evaluation choices for the demonstration, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Prospectively generate circuits and pathways under predefined acceptance criteria

completion_criteria.text: Independent laboratories should test the initially submitted designs using reproducible construction and assay procedures. The evaluation should report all submitted designs and failures, distinguish initial success from success after redesign, and account for computational filtering, experimental selection and the effort required to obtain a working system. Comparisons with strong existing workflows should use comparable resource budgets so that apparent gains cannot be explained simply by additional screening.
completion_criteria.label: Independent testing reports all designs, failures and full resource costs

completion_criteria.text: A convincing result would show reproducible agreement between specified and measured behavior across the declared test domain, with a measurable improvement in reliability or development effort. Practical boundaries should state which hosts, conditions and design classes were demonstrated, where performance degraded, and what application-specific validation remains. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality or automatic portability to untested organisms.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce specified behavior with improved reliability or reduced development effort

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” shares the ambition of predicting function from designed genetic material. BIF-13 concerns circuits and pathways installed in specified existing hosts; BIF-05 addresses complete functional genomes. Success at either scale would not by itself establish success at the other.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” could inform the control of expression, while BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” could inform how interventions propagate through a host. BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” overlaps with predicting cellular responses to a designed subsystem. BIF-13 adds the task of choosing genetic designs that satisfy requested functions; decoding regulation, reconstructing causal relationships and simulating cells remain distinct goals.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-02, “Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence,” BIF-06, “A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions,” and BIF-09, “Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities,” could supply information about candidate components and their interactions. Such predictions could support design, but would not alone establish the behavior of an assembled circuit or pathway inside its host.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” overlaps with automating design, selection and learning from experiments. Its defining ambition is broader autonomous discovery; BIF-13's defining outcome is predictable biological function from an explicit design specification. More generally, BIF-13 connects bioinformatics with synthetic biology, systems biology, metabolic engineering and experimental automation without collapsing those fields into a single capability.

unresolved_issues: The empty freshness record leaves subsequent progress and field-wide availability of the full capability as of 1 November 2026 unresolved.
The supplied evidence does not directly establish the resource-competition and environmental-dependence assertions or quantify their contributions to design failure.
Numerical acceptance thresholds, acceptable failure rates, representative design classes and sufficient host–condition coverage remain to be specified for the proposed demonstration.
The magnitude of any reduction in design–build–test cycles remains unmeasured against comparable existing workflows.
Truncated extraction, pages without extractable text and uninspected figures or omitted material limit assessment of details beyond the supplied review.
Experimental portability beyond the reviewed E. coli assays, broader structural-novelty claims and application-specific performance remain unestablished by this record.

brief.title: Reliable genetic instructions for chosen cell tasks
possible: Researchers could specify how a cell should respond to a signal or how much of a substance it should produce, then obtain genetic instructions that reliably deliver that behavior in a chosen organism and environment.

This would cover genetic circuits, which control cellular responses, and pathways, which produce outputs through linked biological steps. The goal is to predict how the assembled system behaves, including how its parts interact.
why: Biological engineers could spend less effort screening candidates and redesigning systems that miss their targets. A requested function would become a more dependable starting point for building something that works.
That could support more dependable biological production and programmable cellular responses, including systems intended for therapeutic or environmental use.

sources.who: Aditi T. Merchant, Samuel H. King, Eric Nguyen and Brian L. Hie
sources.showed: Evo, an AI model trained on DNA, generated active proteins that block CRISPR, a genetic defense system, and interacting toxins and antidotes. Experiments demonstrated working components and small systems after candidate selection.
sources.quote:
First, we produce several novel 
toxin–antitoxin pairs with high experimental success rates, including 
a toxic gene with no significant sequence similarity to known bacterial 
toxins and a functional RNA antitoxin.
sources.cited_for: Generated genetic instructions can produce active components that work together.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish reliable design of complete circuits and pathways from quantitative requirements.

sources.who: Alec A. K. Nielsen and collaborators
sources.showed: Cello software translated descriptions of circuit behavior into DNA for E. coli bacteria. Most circuits worked correctly in every tested output state without further tuning.
sources.quote:
The DNA sequences were
built as specified with no additional tuning,
requiring 880,000 base pairs of DNA assembly.
sources.cited_for: Automated design can deliver working genetic circuits within a defined organism and operating range.
sources.not_established: The results do not establish broad design of pathways or reliable transfer to other organisms and conditions.

sources.who: Kathleen S. Dreyer, Anh V. Nguyen and collaborators
sources.showed: Their mammalian-cell design framework searched for circuits meeting specified goals. Experimental amplifiers increased output, but predicted output levels did not consistently match measurements. This version is a preprint.
sources.quote: We evaluated the framework for design problems of varying complexity, including programs we describe as an amplifier, signal conditioner, and pulse generator, demonstrating that the algorithm can successfully find optimal circuit designs.
sources.cited_for: Design software can search for mammalian circuits, while experiments expose gaps in its predictions.
sources.not_established: Finding designs in a model does not establish that their measured behavior will reliably meet the requested targets.

shown: Nielsen and colleagues used Cello to turn circuit descriptions into working DNA in E. coli bacteria. Most circuits behaved correctly across every tested input combination without further tuning. This demonstrates automated design within a defined setting.

Merchant and colleagues generated working proteins and interacting toxin–antidote systems with Evo, using filtering and experimental screening. Dreyer and colleagues also tested computer-designed mammalian circuits, but their preprint reports mismatches between predicted and measured output.
missing: Reliable design of interacting circuits and pathways that meet quantitative targets across several organisms and conditions remains to be demonstrated.
Independent tests must count initial failures, redesigns, screening and total effort against comparable existing workflows.
Therapeutic, industrial and environmental uses still need their own demonstrations of performance, stability and suitability.

milestones.label: Circuits and pathways designed against predefined targets
milestones.explanation: Multiple circuits and pathways would have to meet numerical targets across several named organisms and conditions, with robustness and failure limits set before testing. This would test design against explicit requirements.

milestones.label: Independent tests account for every design and its costs
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to report every submitted design, failure, redesign and resource cost, comparing existing methods under matched budgets. This would reveal whether gains depend on extra screening.

milestones.label: Reproducible behavior with better reliability or less development effort
milestones.explanation: Measured behavior would have to reproducibly match specifications, with improved reliability or reduced development effort across a clearly bounded test range. This would establish the capability and where it works.

uncertain: What targets, acceptable failure rates and range of organisms and conditions would make a convincing demonstration?
How much do competition for cellular resources and environmental changes contribute to prediction failures?
How much development effort would predictive design save compared with strong existing methods?

page.title: Predictive design of genetic circuits and metabolic pathways
page.definition: A design framework converts quantitative specifications into DNA for genetic circuits, which process signals, and metabolic pathways, which convert substrates into products. The resulting systems meet those specifications in declared hosts and environments, with component and host interactions included in the predictions.

goal.need: Cello's Escherichia coli study assembled 880,000 base pairs of DNA from automated designs without post-design tuning. Whole-circuit correctness remained below output-state correctness. These results distinguish successful DNA construction and individual responses from correct operation of an assembled genetic system.

figures.caption: Cello correctness results, published on 1 April 2016.
rows: Circuits correct in every output state

statements.quote: enable high-confidence (90%) design of purposeful engineered biological systems at all scales, from molecular to ecosystem level.
statements.context: Goal 2.2 in the NSF-authored cross-cutting section of the federal biotechnology goals report. The report does not operationally define the quoted confidence requirement.

statements.body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
statements.quote: develop a suite of measurement tools that can be used across labs and enable predictive engineering of organisms
statements.context: David Ross, leader of NIST's Engineering Biology Team, states the team's goal.

completion.title: Independent laboratories reproduce specified circuit and pathway functions across host classes.
completion.criterion: One specification-to-DNA framework produces genetic circuits and metabolic pathways whose first builds satisfy externally specified quantitative functions in prokaryotic and eukaryotic hosts under stated environmental conditions. Predictions include component interactions and host effects. Independent laboratories reproduce the specified functions without redesign. Each function uses its published acceptance limits; no common success fraction, prediction-error bound or host panel has been established.
completion.set_by: Atlas; synthesis of published design goals and experimental validation practices, rather than an externally adopted completion protocol.
completion.basis: EBRC's circuit/pathway roadmap, NSF's design goals, NIST's predictive-engineering statement and DARPA Living Foundries were searched for a shared completion protocol. None defines success fractions, prediction-error limits and host coverage together for circuits and pathways. NSF's “high-confidence (90%)” is not operationally defined. This test combines specification-driven design, host interactions and independent replication without assigning a numerical cutoff.

milestones.title: An assembled genetic circuit or pathway exhibits its intended function in a living host.
milestones.criterion: An assembled circuit produces its intended input–output response, or an assembled pathway makes its intended product, in a specified host. Assays use function-specific endpoints. Merchant et al. (19 November 2025) found growth rescue for 5 of 10 selected antitoxins co-expressed with EvoRelE1 in E. coli (3 biological replicates). Kushwaha and Salis (17 July 2015) expressed a three-enzyme neurosporene pathway in E. coli, Pseudomonas putida and Bacillus subtilis (2 measurements per condition). These establish laboratory function, not quantitative design accuracy.
milestones.set_by: Experimental synthetic-biology convention: functional assays of assembled systems, exemplified by the cited circuit and pathway studies. The quoted assay specifically tests bacterial toxin–antitoxin function.
milestones.threshold_quote: Growth curves were analysed to evaluate antitoxin-mediated rescue of growth.

milestones.title: Genetic-system designs incorporate coupled gene expression in prokaryotic hosts.
milestones.criterion: Design circuits or pathways in prokaryotic hosts using models incorporating coupled transcription, translation and mRNA decay. EBRC sets no common error tolerance or success fraction. Huang et al. (24 October 2025) report mean prediction error below 1.4-fold in more than 50 circuit test cases. Their three-enzyme E. coli lycopene pathway yielded 341 ng/ml (6 biological replicates), after context-specific enzyme-expression characterization. These results do not establish general prediction of host effects.
milestones.set_by: Engineering Biology Research Consortium, Engineering Biology (2019), Goal 3, Breakthrough Capability 1, pages 48–49.
milestones.threshold_quote: Incorporate gene expression interactions into predictable design of prokaryotic genetic systems.

milestones.title: Genetic-system designs incorporate coupled gene expression in eukaryotic hosts.
milestones.criterion: Incorporate epigenetic regulation, transcription, translation, mRNA processing and decay into predictive circuit or pathway design in eukaryotic hosts. EBRC supplies no numerical acceptance limits. GCAD (13 February 2026) tested 4 amplifier circuits in HEK293FT cells, each in biological triplicate. All exceeded the reference ON-state output, but initial predicted magnitudes disagreed with measurements; post hoc induction calibration and transcriptional resource-competition modeling accounted for discrepancies. This circuit study does not establish prospective prediction for eukaryotic pathways.
milestones.set_by: Engineering Biology Research Consortium, Engineering Biology (2019), Goal 3, Breakthrough Capability 1, page 49.
milestones.threshold_quote: Incorporate gene expression interactions into predictable design of eukaryotic genetic systems.

not_found: No shared experimental completion protocol covering quantitative circuit and pathway design across prokaryotic and eukaryotic hosts was found.
No operational definition or evaluation protocol for NSF's 90% design-confidence target was found.
The supplied Cello PDF could not be retrieved; the authors' NIST abstract was accessible.
The full text of Peng et al.'s 2022 yeast regulatory-circuit and metabolic-pathway study could not be opened.

results.finding: Five of 10 generated antitoxins rescued growth when co-expressed with EvoRelE1 in E. coli.
results.detail: The type II toxin–antitoxin growth-rescue assay used three biological replicates. The result establishes function, not quantitative design accuracy.
results.quote:
Following co-expression with EvoRelE1, 50% of the Evo-generated 
antitoxin candidates rescued cell growth (Fig. 2d and Extended Data 
Fig. 2e).

results.finding: Of 60 Cello-designed E. coli circuits, 45 performed correctly in every output state.
results.detail: Circuit outputs were measured by flow cytometry. DNA sequences were built without additional tuning.
results.quote:
Of these, 45 circuits performed correctly in every output state (up to 10 regulators and
55 parts), and across all circuits 92% of the output states functioned as predicted.

results.finding: Of 60 Cello-designed E. coli circuits, 45 performed correctly in every output state.

results.detail: A IMPLY B was tested across three T2 lines and NAND across four. GFP fluorescence was measured in roots after chemical induction.

results.finding: 73 crtEBI pathway variants in E. coli produced neurosporene at 3.3–196 µg/gDCW/h.
results.detail: Neurosporene was measured by acetone extraction and spectrophotometry after a 7-hour post-induction culture. Figure 4 reports at least three measurements.

results.finding: Engineered S. cerevisiae CSY1296 produced 1.0 μg/L scopolamine de novo; assays used at least 3 replicates.
results.detail: The strain contained all five pathway modules. Metabolites in culture supernatant were measured by LC-MS/MS.

results.finding: An E. coli genetic circuit retained nearly 95% of its output under ribosome competition, across 3 biological replicates.
results.detail: The model used to design the feedback controller incorporated transcription, translation and mRNA decay. The result measures robustness to a resource competitor; it does not establish general prediction of host effects.
